title: Subcomplex of an abstract cell complex
body_html:
Subcomplex

Let $X$ be an [[abstract cell complex|node:abstract_cell_complex.abstract_cell_complex]]. A subcomplex of $X$ is a subset $S \subseteq X$ that is face-closed: if $F \in S$ and $E \preceq F$ then $E \in S$.

That is, whenever $S$ contains a cell it contains every one of that cell's faces. Equivalently, $S$ is a down-set of the face poset $X$.

If $X$ carries a cellular $G$-action (Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex), the setwise stabiliser of a subcomplex $S$ is

$$ \Stab_G(S) := \{ g \in G : g \cdot S = S \} = \{ g \in G : \forall E \in X, \ g \cdot E \in S \iff E \in S \}. $$

The iff form emphasises that $g \in \Stab_G(S)$ requires both $g \cdot S \subseteq S$ and $g^{-1} \cdot S \subseteq S$; either inclusion alone is not enough for a subgroup structure.

Downstream uses

  • The setwise stabiliser is the coarsest choice of "distinguished subgroup" in a quasi-fundamental domain Quasi-fundamental domain; sharper QFDs use a strictly smaller subgroup.
  • The image of the canonical induction embedding is a subcomplex — CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X'.
  • Face-closedness of the QFD subcomplex is what lets the reverse induction construction lift ambient face relations back to $S$; see Recovering the induction data from a quasi-fundamental domain.

Lean formalization

```lean structure Subcomplex (X : Type*) [PartialOrder X] where carrier : Set X face_closed' : ∀ {E F : X}, E ≤ F → F ∈ carrier → E ∈ carrier

instance : SetLike (Subcomplex X) X where coe S := S.carrier coe_injective' := fun S T h => by cases S; cases T; congr

theorem face_closed (S : Subcomplex X) {E F : X} (hEF : E ≤ F) (hF : F ∈ S) : E ∈ S := S.face_closed' hEF hF ```

The Subcomplex type is modelled after mathlib's Subgroup / Submonoid idiom: a carrier : Set X field plus a SetLike instance gives the usual $E \in S$ notation and coercion to Set X. The primed field face_closed' is the raw structure axiom; the user-facing lemma face_closed restates it in terms of $\in$.
